title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch E/F Voltage Correlation
plain: Two position sensors that should agree with each other (sensors E and F) are giving different readings. The computer uses this check to make sure the throttle is safe.
symptoms: Reduced engine power or limp mode
Poor or no response to the gas pedal

causes.name: Failing throttle body or pedal position sensor
Wiring or connector problem
Shared 5-volt reference circuit shorted by another sensor
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the throttle body and pedal connectors for corrosion or loose pins
Watch both sensor readings together in live data while moving the throttle or pedal
fix: Repair wiring or connector problems; otherwise replace the throttle body or pedal assembly, whichever holds the two sensors.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Throttle Control Circuit Low
plain: The control circuit for the EGR throttle valve is reading low voltage. This part restricts intake air on some diesels to help pull exhaust gas back into the engine. A wire shorted to ground or a shorted part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Possible rough running or shutdown shudder on diesels

causes.name: Control wire shorted to ground
Internally shorted EGR throttle valve
Damaged connector
Engine computer driver problem (rare)

checks: Check the EGR throttle valve wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the EGR throttle valve resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the EGR throttle valve.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Throttle Control Circuit High
plain: The control circuit for the EGR throttle valve is reading high voltage. This part restricts intake air on some diesels to help pull exhaust gas back into the engine. A wire shorted to power, an open circuit or a failed part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Possible rough running or shutdown shudder on diesels

causes.name: Failed EGR throttle valve
Control wire shorted to a power source
Open circuit or corroded connector
Engine computer driver problem (rare)

checks: Check the EGR throttle valve wiring for shorts to other wires
Measure the EGR throttle valve resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the EGR throttle valve.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Vent Control Circuit/Open
plain: The engine computer can't properly control the EGR vent solenoid, which vents vacuum from the EGR valve so it can close. It sees an open or broken circuit, often from wiring, a connector or the part itself.
symptoms: Possible rough idle if the EGR valve stays open

causes.name: Failed EGR vent solenoid
Broken wire or unplugged connector
Blown fuse or bad relay feeding the circuit
Engine computer driver problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the EGR vent solenoid connector and wiring
Check for power at the connector and measure the part's resistance
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the EGR vent solenoid.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation Vent Control Circuit Low
plain: The control circuit for the EGR vent solenoid is reading low voltage. This part vents vacuum from the EGR valve so it can close. A wire shorted to ground or a shorted part is the usual reason.
symptoms: Possible rough idle if the EGR valve stays open

causes.name: Control wire shorted to ground
Internally shorted EGR vent solenoid
Damaged connector
Engine computer driver problem (rare)

checks: Check the EGR vent solenoid wiring for rubbed-through insulation
Measure the EGR vent solenoid resistance and compare with spec
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the EGR vent solenoid.

title: Fuel Injector Group "A" Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
plain: The power supply that feeds a group of fuel injectors (group A) has lost its power feed. Those injectors may not fire properly, causing misfires or rough running.

causes.name: Blown fuse or failed injector power relay
Damaged injector supply wiring or connector
Shorted fuel injector pulling the circuit down
Engine computer driver problem

checks: Check the injector fuses and relay
Check for supply voltage at each injector in the group
fix: Replace a blown fuse or bad relay and repair the wiring or shorted injector that caused it.

cost.job: Repair injector supply wiring or relay

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "B"
plain: The engine computer has found a problem in the circuit for the vehicle speed sensor B, which measures how fast the vehicle is going (often the transmission output speed). It usually points to wiring, a connector or the sensor itself.

causes.name: Faulty vehicle speed sensor B
Damaged, corroded or unplugged connector
Broken or chafed wiring
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the speed sensor connector and wiring for damage or corrosion
Check the sensor power, ground and signal with a meter
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the vehicle speed sensor B.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "B" Range/Performance
plain: The vehicle speed sensor B is giving readings that don't make sense compared with what the computer expects. This sensor measures how fast the vehicle is going (often the transmission output speed). The sensor may be failing or the system it watches may have a real problem.

causes.name: Failing or out-of-calibration vehicle speed sensor B
Damaged tone ring or metal debris on the sensor tip
High resistance in the wiring or connector

checks: Compare the speed sensor reading with related sensors in live data
Check wiring and connector for corrosion or looseness
fix: Confirm the system itself is working, then replace the vehicle speed sensor B if its readings are off.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "B" Circuit Low
plain: The signal from the vehicle speed sensor B is lower than the computer expects. This sensor measures how fast the vehicle is going (often the transmission output speed). A wire shorted to ground or a failed sensor is the usual reason.

causes.name: Signal or reference wire shorted to ground
Failed vehicle speed sensor B
Corroded or damaged connector
Engine computer problem (rare)

checks: Inspect the speed sensor wiring for rubbed-through or pinched spots
Unplug the sensor and see if the reading changes, which helps separate wiring from sensor
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the vehicle speed sensor B.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "B" Intermittent/Erratic
plain: The signal from the vehicle speed sensor B keeps dropping out or jumping around. This sensor measures how fast the vehicle is going (often the transmission output speed). A loose connection or a damaged wire is the usual reason.

causes.name: Loose or corroded connector
Chafed wire that opens or shorts as the engine moves
Failing vehicle speed sensor B

checks: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching live data for dropouts
Inspect the speed sensor wiring along its whole route
fix: Repair any damaged wiring or connector first; if the circuit tests good, replace the vehicle speed sensor B.

title: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A"/"B" Correlation
plain: The vehicle has two speed sensors and their readings don't agree. One sensor or its wiring is usually giving a bad signal.
symptoms: ABS or traction light may come on

causes.name: Failing speed sensor A or B
Damaged wiring or connector at a speed sensor
Metal debris on a sensor tip or damaged tone ring
Wrong tire sizes front to rear

checks: Compare both speed readings in live data while driving
Inspect both sensors, connectors and wiring
fix: Replace the sensor that reads wrong and repair any wiring damage.

title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Maximum Stop Performance
plain: Throttle or pedal position sensor A isn't reading what the computer expects when the throttle or pedal is fully pressed. The sensor may be worn or the pedal may not be reaching full travel.
symptoms: Possible reduced power at full throttle

causes.name: Worn throttle or pedal position sensor
Floor mat or object blocking full pedal travel
Throttle body not opening fully
Wiring or connector problem

checks: Make sure nothing blocks the pedal and that it reaches full travel
Watch sensor readings at full pedal in live data
fix: Clear any obstruction; replace the pedal or throttle body if its sensor reads wrong at full travel.

Blown fuse or bad relay feeding the circuit

Check for power at the connector and measure the part's resistance
fix: Repair any wiring fault first; if the wiring tests good, replace the exhaust pressure regulator vent solenoid.

title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Sudden High Airflow Detected
plain: The computer has seen a sudden jump in airflow that doesn't match the throttle position. It may limit engine power to stay safe.

causes.name: Large vacuum or intake air leak
Faulty mass airflow sensor
Throttle body sticking or worn
Wiring problem at the throttle or airflow sensor

checks: Inspect the air intake ducts, filter and vacuum hoses
Compare airflow and throttle readings in live data
fix: Fix air leaks or restrictions and clean or replace the airflow sensor or throttle body as testing shows.

title: Throttle Actuator Control System - High Airflow Detected

causes.name: Large vacuum or intake air leak
Faulty mass airflow sensor
Throttle body sticking or worn
Wiring problem at the throttle or airflow sensor

checks: Inspect the air intake ducts, filter and vacuum hoses

fix: Fix air leaks or restrictions and clean or replace the airflow sensor or throttle body as testing shows.

Throttle body sticking or worn
Wiring problem at the throttle or airflow sensor

checks: Inspect the air intake ducts, filter and vacuum hoses
Compare airflow and throttle readings in live data
fix: Fix air leaks or restrictions and clean or replace the airflow sensor or throttle body as testing shows.

checks: Inspect the air intake ducts, filter and vacuum hoses

title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Idle Position Not Learned
plain: The computer hasn't learned the throttle's resting (idle) position. This often happens after a battery disconnect, throttle cleaning or replacement.

causes.name: Throttle idle relearn not completed after battery or throttle work
Dirty throttle body
Failing throttle body
Wiring or connector problem

checks: Perform the throttle relearn procedure for your vehicle
Clean the throttle body if it is dirty
fix: Run the idle relearn; replace the throttle body only if it fails to learn after cleaning.

title: System Too Lean Off Idle Bank 1
plain: The engine on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) is running too lean when driving just above idle, and the computer has reached the limit of what it can correct. Too much air or too little fuel is getting in.

causes.name: Vacuum leak (cracked hose, intake gasket or PCV valve)
Dirty or faulty mass airflow (MAF) sensor
Leaking intake manifold gasket
Low fuel pressure or weak fuel pump
Exhaust leak before the front oxygen sensor

checks: Listen and smoke-test for vacuum leaks
Inspect and clean the MAF sensor
Check fuel trims at idle and at higher RPM
fix: Find and repair the leak or fuel delivery problem; replacing parts without testing rarely fixes it.

cost.job: Find and repair vacuum leak (hose or intake gasket)

title: System Too Rich Off Idle Bank 1
plain: The engine on bank 1 (the side of the engine with cylinder 1) is running too rich when driving just above idle, and the computer has reached the limit of what it can correct. Too much fuel or too little air is getting in.

causes.name: Leaking or stuck-open fuel injector
Fuel pressure too high (bad regulator)
Faulty mass airflow (MAF) or upstream oxygen sensor
Clogged air filter or intake

checks: Check fuel pressure and look for a leaking injector
Inspect the air filter and MAF sensor
fix: Find the source of extra fuel (injector, pressure regulator or sensor) and repair it.

title: System Too Lean Off Idle Bank 2
plain: The engine on bank 2 (the side of the engine opposite cylinder 1) is running too lean when driving just above idle, and the computer has reached the limit of what it can correct. Too much air or too little fuel is getting in.

causes.name: Vacuum leak (cracked hose, intake gasket or PCV valve)
Dirty or faulty mass airflow (MAF) sensor
Leaking intake manifold gasket
Low fuel pressure or weak fuel pump

checks: Listen and smoke-test for vacuum leaks
Inspect and clean the MAF sensor
fix: Find and repair the leak or fuel delivery problem; replacing parts without testing rarely fixes it.
